messages:
sam: Alert from Cloud Logging: a batch of GCS objects created without our CMEK metadata in gs://redwood-backups-legacy. Query shows 236 objects from last deploy window.
rachel: which pipeline wrote that bucket? backup-uploader-gcs or the transfer service?
diego: that was me — I pushed a terraform update yesterday to add CMEK to the new bucket but I missed the legacy bucket resource in the module. I think new objects fell back to Google-managed keys.
sam: example object: snapshots/tenant-77/2026-03-01/db.dump.gz. `gsutil ls -L` shows "Customer-managed encryption: No" and no `x-redwood-cmek-id` metadata.
irene: are any restores failing or public ACLs set? immediate risk?
sam: restores OK (GCS will decrypt with GMK), but this violates our compliance requirement (customer CMEK) and audit policy. No public ACLs detected so far.
diego: double oof. I also changed the backup-uploader SA binding in the same PR to a new service account, and I didn't add the `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` binding for that SA. So even if we retroactively tried re-encrypt, the SA wouldn't have the KMS perms.
oncall: can we block further writes to that bucket until we fix it?
rachel: yes — remove writer role from the uploader SA on the bucket or add a bucket policy only allowing CMEK writes. Quick mitigation first.
sam: encops-bot, open incident for this and tag compliance + backups please.
encops-bot: incident created INC-2026-0501. Triage channel: #inc-INC-2026-0501. Tags: encryption, gcs, backups, terraform.
diego: mitigation plan: 1) revoke writer role from backup-uploader SA on legacy bucket (temp); 2) run a re-encrypt job that downloads each object and re-uploads with CMEK; 3) patch terraform to include legacy bucket key binding and add pre-deploy lint that asserts CMEK present; 4) add log alert for objects created without `x-redwood-cmek-id`.
irene: add RBAC audit steps: search Cloud Audit Logs for `SetIamPolicy` changes on the KMS key ring and for `projects.trustedServiceAccounts` bindings in the timeframe. Also verify no other service accounts were given writer perms.
sam: I ran a quick audit: 1723452000-1723458000 shows 236 objects created by `serviceAccount:backup-uploader@infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com` and a SetIamPolicy on the bucket at 1723452400 by diego.
rachel: do we have any Gaussian retention or immutability that prevents reuploading? need to check lifecycle rules. If retention lock present, we might need legal signoff.
diego: lifecycle rules OK, no retention hold. I'll prepare the re-encrypt job. Need to decide runner: do we run from a GCE worker with a temporary SA that has KMS encrypt permissions?
irene: yes, create a short-lived privileged SA for the task, use Workload Identity or token exchange, run job from isolated GCP project, ensure Cloud Audit Logs are enabled and exported. Put results to s3://redwood-incidents/INC-2026-0501/rekey-report.csv or gs://redwood-incidents.
sam: sample re-encrypt command for one object: 

```
gsutil cp gs://redwood-backups-legacy/snapshots/tenant-77/2026-03-01/db.dump.gz /tmp/db.dump.gz
gsutil -o GoogleCSEK:kms_key=projects/myproj/locations/global/keyRings/backups/cryptoKeys/tenant-cmek cp /tmp/db.dump.gz gs://redwood-backups-legacy/snapshots/tenant-77/2026-03-01/db.dump.gz
```
Note: we need `kms_key` and the SA to have `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter`.
oncall: I'll stand up a runner and coordinate windows with ops if reuploads might impact restores.
rachel: followup tasks: SEC-901 (terraform CMEK lint), SEC-902 (log alert for missing cmek metadata on object creation), OP-339 (runbook update for rekey job).
diego: I ran `gsutil ls -L gs://redwood-backups-legacy/snapshots/tenant-77/2026-03-01/ | grep "Customer-managed encryption"` — output: "Customer-managed encryption: No" for several objects. Confirmed.
encops-bot: update: writer binding revoked at 1723456900. Re-encrypt job queued at 1723457300.
sam: timeline: revoke in 5m, runner/credentials ready in 25m, re-encrypt start in 40m, estimated completion 3h (batched). I'll post progress to INC-2026-0501.
irene: low risk of exfil since objects remained private, but this is a compliance breach. We'll need a short postmortem and to notify compliance.
diego: I'll open the terraform patch PR and include the pre-deploy linter hook. Sorry team.
rachel: thanks. once re-encrypt completes we'll run an audit query to ensure `kms:Encrypt` was used and metadata present. Keep oncall posted.
encops-bot: incident status: mitigation in progress.
